Indian

GRADING FOR DHUPA KERNELS FOR OIL MILLING

0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 16 November 1981 after the draft finalized by the Oils and Oilsccds Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council and the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 DHUPA kernels are obtained from seed of DHUPA ( Vateriu in&z Linn. ) tree. DHUPA trees grow mostly in moist evergreen forests in the Western Ghats and foothills from North Kanara ( Karnataka ) to Keraln through the Glznt forests of South Kanara, Coorg, M&bar and Coimbatore. It is also occasionally found in deciduous forests adjoining rivers in the aforementioned areas. Apart from the Chats, DHUPA trees are also found on the Deccan Plateau and along the Arabian sea-coast, the altitudinal range being from 60 to 1 220 metres. DHUPA trees have also been extensively planted as an avenue tree in parts of Karnataka and Kerala States. The flowering time is from January to March and fruits ripen from May to July. The fruits are fleshy, wingless, about 50 to 60 mm long and contain one large seed. 0.3 DHUPA kernels contain 16 to 25 percent of a pale-yellow fat having tallow-like consistency, which turns white on standing. The fat is known by a number of names, such as Malabar tallow, Piney tallow and DHCJPA tallow. The fat derived from DHUPA kernels is suitable for soap and candle making. The refined fat is suitable for edible purpose. It has good substitute or extender after proper potential for use as cocoa butter It has also good prospects for use in yarn sizing. processing. 0.4 The requirements 1s :x879-1978*.
